title: Yara and the Summer
premise: Ulyana Dravenmoor has built her ghostwriting career on invisibility, and her newest commission—memoirs for celebrated vintner Elias Marchetti—is her riskiest job yet. But when a lost letter, written eleven years ago and never delivered, resurfaces in the vineyard's cellar, Ulyana realizes the man she once loved and abandoned is the rival author she's been secretly outshining, and that her silence cost them both everything. As the first harvest approaches, she must choose between exposing the truth that could destroy her career and confessing the lie that has kept her safe, ultimately surrendering her anonymity and her byline to win back the person who finally sees her. The book ends with the memoir published under his name and hers, and the two of them pressing the season's first wine together as equals.
about_author: Dominic Fairweather spent a decade writing other people's stories before finding the courage to sign his own. He lives near a working vineyard and swears the best romances ferment slowly.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Guest House
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives at Marchetti Vineyard under a false name to ghostwrite Elias Marchetti's memoirs, determined to remain invisible as always. Through her POV, we feel the familiar comfort of erasure and a flicker of dread when Elias greets her with an unsettling, searching look. Emotional beat: guarded anticipation, the safety of disguise beginning to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Interviews at Dusk
chapters.summary: In Elias's POV, the evening interview sessions begin, and he finds himself telling Ulyana things he's never said aloud—especially about a woman who vanished eleven years ago. Ulyana, listening from behind her recorder, recognizes her own story being told back to her. Emotional beat: vertigo and guilt, intimacy building on a foundation of concealment.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: While cataloging the cellar for a memoir chapter, Ulyana discovers a water-stained, undelivered letter postmarked eleven years ago—her own handwriting, her own farewell. Her POV carries the shock of confronting the lie that shaped two lives. Emotional beat: panic and grief colliding, the past physically unearthed.

chapters.title: The Rival's Byline
chapters.summary: Elias's POV reveals his motive for the memoir: reclaiming his story from 'A. Wren,' the anonymous author whose bestselling novel fictionalized and betrayed their shared past. Ulyana realizes she is his rival, and that her career was built on his heartbreak. Emotional beat: shame sharpened into self-defense, as loyalty to her career wars with the truth.

chapters.title: First Light, Last Harvest
chapters.summary: Working side by side during pre-harvest preparations, Ulyana and Elias grow closer, trading confessions that stop just short of the truth. Her POV traces the dangerous warmth of being known almost entirely. Emotional beat: tender, doomed happiness—love flourishing precisely where the lie is deepest.

chapters.title: A Question of Loyalty
chapters.summary: Elias's editor demands the memoir expose 'A. Wren' as a plagiarist, and Elias asks Ulyana, as his confidante, to help him find proof. Her POV splits between protecting her identity and protecting him from a justice that would wound them both. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth, the noose tightening.

chapters.title: The Letter, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Elias finally reads the old letter and recognizes the handwriting; in his POV, eleven years of grief curdle into betrayal as he realizes his ghostwriter and his lost love are the same person. He says nothing—but the vineyard's warmth turns cold. Emotional beat: devastation held in silence, trust fracturing in real time.

chapters.title: Storm Before the Pickers
chapters.summary: On the eve of harvest, a storm threatens the grapes and the truth breaks: Ulyana confesses everything—the letter, the novel, the years of hiding. Alternating POV climaxes in a raw confrontation where Elias demands to know if anything she felt was real. Emotional beat: the climax, love and fury indistinguishable in the rain.

chapters.title: Justice, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Ulyana publicly claims authorship of 'A. Wren's' novel, sacrificing her anonymity and her career to clear Elias's name and set the record straight. His POV follows her press statement and the industry fallout, realizing she chose truth over the career that saved her. Emotional beat: costly redemption, justice achieved outside any law.

chapters.title: The First Pour
chapters.summary: At the harvest festival, the memoir is published with both their names on the cover, and Elias pours Ulyana the first glass of the vintage they saved together. Her POV closes the arc: invisibility traded for being truly seen, second chances finally arriving on time. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution and open-hearted beginning.
